texts.arguments: 3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the license was issued in the name of the proprietor and the petitioner cannot be held criminally liable under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. He submits that the case against the petitioner is not made out under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. 4. The learned counsel for the respondent State submits that this petitioner was named as licensee which is evident from the license brought on the record by way of filing counter affidavit. He submits that the said license was renewed from 27.4.2007 to 31.3.2012 and the said allegations are Tuhin Mukherjee vs The State Of Jharkhand And Another .... ... on 5 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138179461/ 1 of the year 2009. He submits that during that period the petitioner was the licensee. On these grounds he submits that no case of interference is made out. 5. It appears that there are allegations against the petitioner and others of Paneer and R-pure haldi power were not found to be in consonance with the standard of quality laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the analyst report is there dated 18.04.2009.
